descriptor: A shaggy-coated great ape living in silverback-led families on the cloud-forested volcanoes of central Africa.

physical.fact: Its fur is longer and thicker than other gorillas', helping it cope with cold, high mountain forests.

range.summary: Two isolated populations: the Virunga volcanoes shared by DRC, Rwanda and Uganda, and Bwindi-Sarambwe in Uganda and DRC.

regions.name: Mikeno sector, DRC
regions.note: DRC's Mikeno sector, in Africa's first national park, is part of the Virunga gorillas' home.

regions.name: Volcanoes NP, Rwanda
regions.note: Rwanda's Volcanoes park, where gorillas have been studied since Dian Fossey began in 1967.

regions.name: Mgahinga, Uganda
regions.note: Mgahinga's Nyakagezi group crosses freely between Uganda, Rwanda and DRC.

regions.name: Bwindi
regions.note: Bwindi's 2011 census found at least 400 gorillas, up from 302 counted in 2006.

regions.name: Sarambwe, DRC
regions.note: DRC's small Sarambwe reserve adjoins Bwindi and shares its gorilla population.

regions.name: Pyrethrum clearance
regions.note: Between 1969 and 1973, part of Rwanda's Volcanoes park was cleared to grow pyrethrum.

regions.name: Mikeno clearance
regions.note: In 2004 settlers illegally cleared about 15 square km of prime gorilla forest in the Mikeno sector.

source.label: IUCN Red List: Gorilla beringei ssp. beringei (Hickey et al. 2020)

rangeHistory.note: Mountain gorillas have never been reintroduced; their range changes are habitat losses at the edge of two small protected blocks.

population.unit: mountain gorillas in the Virunga Massif

source.label: Greater Virunga Transboundary Collaboration census 2015-2016, with earlier censuses (Aveling & Harcourt 1984; Kalpers et al. 2003)

population.note: The 1973 and 1981 values are census estimates allowing for undercounting, and 2000 is a minimum count. Bwindi-Sarambwe held 459 gorillas in 2018, bringing the world total to 1,063.

threats.title: Human-borne disease
threats.detail: Gorillas catch respiratory infections from people, and outbreaks can kill several in a group.

threats.title: Snares
threats.detail: Traps set for antelope maim and kill gorillas, especially young ones.

threats.title: Tiny, isolated range
threats.detail: The whole subspecies lives in two forest islands surrounded by dense farmland.

threats.title: Armed conflict
threats.detail: Fighting in eastern DRC has repeatedly cut off patrols and killed rangers in Virunga.

source.label: IUCN Red List: Gorilla beringei ssp. beringei

places.name: Volcanoes National Park
places.note: Habituated families on bamboo slopes, where Dian Fossey worked.

places.name: Bwindi Impenetrable National Park
places.note: Steep rainforest holding nearly half of all mountain gorillas.

places.name: Mgahinga Gorilla National Park
places.note: Uganda's slice of the Virungas, with one habituated group.

places.name: Virunga National Park (Mikeno sector)
places.note: Africa's oldest national park. Check security advice before travel.

sightings.tip: The dry seasons, June to September and December to February, make steep trails less muddy and treks shorter, though gorillas can be seen year-round.

actions.title: Buy a trekking permit
actions.detail: Permit fees fund rangers, and a share goes to communities living around the parks.

actions.title: Do not trek when sick
actions.detail: Stay home with a cold or flu, wear a mask and keep at least 7 m away.

actions.title: Recycle old phones
actions.detail: Recycling cuts demand for coltan, whose mining has damaged gorilla habitat in eastern DRC.

actions.title: Fund veterinary care
actions.detail: Field vets who remove snares and treat illness have helped drive the recovery.

summary.text: The mountain gorilla is one of the two subspecies of the eastern gorilla. It is listed as endangered by the IUCN as of 2018.
